title: Merge Two Sorted Id Ledgers
statement:
Two warehouses each keep a ledger: a list of [id, amount] rows. Within one ledger every id appears at most once, and the rows are sorted by id in increasing order.

Combine them into one ledger. Every id that appears in either input appears once in the output, with the sum of its amounts (an id missing from one ledger counts as 0 there). Return the rows sorted by id in increasing order.

examples.why: Id 3 is in both, so its amounts add to 7. The rest are copied over in id order.
No shared ids. The result simply interleaves the two lists in id order.
b's first id is the smallest overall, so the output can start from either list.

constraints: Ids are strictly increasing within each ledger
hints: Both lists are already sorted by id. Which classic step of merge sort does this look like?
Walk both lists with one pointer each. Take the row with the smaller id; if the ids are equal, add the amounts and advance both.
When one list runs out, copy the rest of the other.

explain.intuition:
This is the merge step of merge sort with one twist. Keep a pointer into each ledger. At each step the smaller current id is the next id of the output, because everything later in either list is larger. If both pointers sit on the same id, write one row with the summed amount and move both.

A hash map from id to total also works, but then you must sort the keys at the end, paying O(n log n) for an order the inputs already gave you.
steps: While both lists have rows: if a[i]'s id is smaller, copy it and move i; if b[j]'s id is smaller, copy it and move j; if they are equal, push [id, a[i][1] + b[j][1]] and move both.
Copy whatever remains of a, then of b.
pitfalls: Moving only one pointer on equal ids, which writes the same id twice.
Forgetting the tail of the longer list once the shorter one runs out.
Pushing the input row objects themselves and then changing their amount, which also changes the caller's data.

solutions.title: Hash map and sort
solutions.idea: Add every amount into a map keyed by id, then sort the ids.

solutions.title: Two-pointer merge
solutions.idea: Both ledgers are sorted, so the next output row always comes from the front of one of them.

followups: Merge k sorted ledgers instead of two. What keeps it efficient?
